author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: A patient Fed, a soft October payrolls print and a 27 bps five-observation fall in the 10Y yield turned higher-for-longer into a peak-rates rally (S&P 500 +5.85% over five sessions, VIX 14.91, DXY 105.02), but the curve is still inverted and growth evidence outside the US is weak, so the move is a rate trade rather than a growth trade. Lean into quality duration-sensitive equities (AI semis, GLP-1 leaders, regulated and nuclear utilities, net-lease REITs) and Polish equities, stay underweight China beta, European autos and global-cycle machinery, and treat Australia's pending RBA hike and Poland's budget hole as the main policy risks.
sources_policy: Facts come only from the 2023-11-06 frozen feed (published before 2023-11-06T00:00Z) and the 2023-11-06 market card. Company news/previews within 7 days, company results within 14 days, macro releases and policy baselines within 35 days. Every number traces to the card or to a headline cited in the same part. Spot-FX levels and returns are not quoted; currency direction comes from cited headlines only. Pending events (RBA meeting, Biden-Xi meeting, spot bitcoin ETF decisions, WeWork filing) are described from previews without asserting outcomes. No later-dated feeds, cards, specs or knowledge were used.
